messages:
Samir: Quick sync — follow-ups from the KV-cache OOM postmortem. We need clear owners, timelines, and which quick mitigations go live this week.
Anya: I can take the profiling + root-cause task. Will run heap/kv snapshots across the canary fleet and produce a flamegraph. ETA EOW (Fri). :white_check_mark:
Javier: I'll own eviction/soft-limit changes and config rollout. Thinking: reduce shard soft_limit to 0.75*current and enable aggressive LRU for cold prefixes. Can do a staged rollout tomorrow.
Priya: I'll own telemetry + alerts: add a ServiceLevel for shard-evictions/sec and a regression alert when fragmentation rises > 15% over baseline. Will also add a dashboard cell for per-model kv-residency.
Samir: Good. Anya — please capture sample commands and locations for artifacts. Javier — link the proposed config and canary plan. Priya — add alert thresholds and playbook steps.
Anya: Profiling plan (short):
```
# on canary
run_kv_snapshot --shard=all --out=/tmp/snap-$(date +%s).prof
python3 -m flamegraph /tmp/snap-*.prof > artifacts/flame-$(date +%Y%m%d).svg
```
I'll upload artifacts to the postmortem doc.
Javier: Config diff I'll deploy as canary in two waves (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with 15m observation windows. Diff snippet: 
```
shard: { soft_limit: 0.75, eviction_policy: "lru_aggressive", slab_compact_interval_s: 3600 }
```
If eviction rate drops but tail latency spikes, we roll back.
Priya: Alert runbook stub:
- Trigger: fragmentation > 15% OR evictions/sec > 100 for 10m
- Pager: eng-runtime oncall
- Mitigation: temporarily throttle writer clients, escalate to infra for immediate reclaim, enable emergency GC (see playbook).
Samir: Who owns the emergency GC toggle and where is the runbook? We need a safe rollback path.
Anya: I added an emergency GC toggle to the runbook (link in the postmortem doc). I'm the owner for responding to profiling findings.
Javier: I can add rollback automation to the canary job to revert config and notify oncall automatically. Will push a PR in the morning.
Priya: I'll add synthetic tests: allocate/evict cycles on staging to validate that soft_limit 0.75 + aggressive LRU holds under write-heavy patterns. Plan to run nightly for a week.
Samir: Timeline recap:
- Profiling artifacts (Anya) — by Fri EOD
- Canary config & automation (Javier) — deploy tomorrow morning + PR for rollback automation
- Alerts + dashboard (Priya) — by Thu EOD; include playbook steps and runbook links
- Quick mitigation (soft_limit change) — staged rollout tomorrow, abort on latency regressions
If anything slips, tag me and assign a blocker in the postmortem doc.
Anya: One noted recurring pattern — large prefix churn correlates with high resident set fragmentation. I suspect leaking references in prefix index warmers. I'll add candidate stack traces.
Javier: Noted. Also will add an option to temporarily disable prefix warmers per-model as a short-term mitigation.
Priya: I'll create a weekly recurring triage agenda for memory/KV regressions and add rotation owners. First recurring meeting Thurs next week.
Samir: Sounds good. Can we capture owners and due dates in the postmortem checklist so CS/SEs can track?
Anya: Done — added a checklist section and pinged the doc with owners + links.
eng-oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: "KV OOM followups check-in" on 2026-03-26 10:00 UTC — attendees: eng-runtime.
Javier: Quick note — we should also add an integration test that ramps sequence length to catch GC pressure induced by long-lived KV entries. I'll draft test today.
Priya: ACK. I'll wire the test outputs into the dashboard.
Samir: Thanks team. I'll close out any loose threads in the doc and run the first triage on Thursday. If we see a regression after the canary, follow the rollback automation immediately and page. :pray:
